description:
We are NINA, a multidisciplinary team of developers specializing in AI, data science, and full-stack software development. Our mission is to transform NASA satellite data (MODIS and VIIRS) into actionable insights that help protect our planet.

Somos NINA, un equipo de desarrolladores especializados en IA, ciencia de datos y software full-stack. Buscamos transformar datos satelitales de NASA (MODIS y VIIRS) en conocimiento útil para proteger el planeta.
summary:
NINA is a satellite fire-monitoring platform that creates a consistent 25-year record of fire activity across Peru by harmonizing observations from MODIS and VIIRS. Different satellite sensors can report significantly different hotspot counts for the same conditions, creating artificial trends that make it difficult to determine whether a fire season is truly unusual. NINA addresses this challenge through a calibration methodology that makes observations comparable across sensors and years.

The platform allows users to explore historical fire activity by region or custom area, identify unusual patterns, compare current activity against historical baselines, and examine the gap between satellite detections and officially reported emergencies.

By transforming fragmented satellite observations into accessible, reproducible evidence, NINA supports better-informed environmental monitoring, disaster preparedness, public accountability, and research in Peru and beyond.
details:
What does it do?

NINA keeps one consistent 25-year record of satellite-detected fire activity across sensor changes, so anyone can see whether a fire season is unusual, where, and where burning goes unreported. Peru's satellite fire record broke in 2012: when VIIRS arrived, September detections jumped ×4.5 in raw pixels without any real change in fire. After NINA's harmonization the same comparison gives ×1.04. The record is breaking again now: S-NPP stopped delivering data on 2 November 2026, and NASA has announced that MODIS Terra and Aqua will be retired.

Repository: https://github.com/Abraham-ch/Nina

Presentation: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NuzrjOWYajKoIldTTjJAfU5EHOAhkovu/view?usp=sharing

NINA:

  • Harmonizes MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20) active-fire detections into a single unit: VIIRS-equivalent active cell-days.
  • Shows a monthly fire calendar (years × months), anomalies against the historical median, and a ranking of years for Peru, its departments, any country, or a custom polygon drawn on a 3D globe.
  • Compares the harmonized series with the original observations of each satellite (NOAA-21 included), side by side on the map.
  • Contrasts detected activity with forest-fire emergencies reported to INDECI. In 2024, Ucayali, San Martín and Loreto held 46 % of the activity detected in Peru but only 7 % of reported emergencies.
  • Exports CSV/ZIP files that include the FIRMS citation, method version, filters and generation date.

How does it work?

  1. Acquisition: standard (archive) and near-real-time detections come from NASA FIRMS. Ingestion validates every row; rejected rows are counted with a reason, never silently dropped. When standard data exist for the same satellite and day, they supersede the NRT data. Landsat is excluded.
  2. Common unit: detections are aggregated into H3 cells of about 5 km² per day. Counting active cells instead of pixels shrinks the resolution gap between 1 km MODIS and 375 m VIIRS.
  3. Calibration: a VIIRS S-NPP/MODIS ratio is fitted per country × biome (RESOLVE Ecoregions) × calendar month × sampling regime, trained only on standard-quality data from the 2012–2025 overlap. NOAA-20 is bridged to S-NPP the same way, which keeps the series going after S-NPP's end.
  4. Validation: leave-one-year-out validation over 2012–2025 in five countries on four continents (Peru, Brazil, Australia, Indonesia, USA). For Peru, the out-of-sample total bias is +0.4 %. As an independent check, INPE's MODIS Aqua series agrees with NINA year to year with r = 0.95 (2012–2025).
  5. Honest gaps: days without valid data are shown as missing, never as zero, and domains that fail validation are not shown.
  6. Delivery: a web atlas with a 3D globe, a calendar, a sensor-comparison lab and an evidence assistant, in English and Spanish.

Benefits and intended impact

  • For institutions: CENEPRED, SERFOR, regional governments and the Defensoría get a multi-year input that does not jump in 2012 or in 2026. In September 2024, the harmonized record showed activity at 1.6× the median on the day of the emergency decree, and it had been above every previous year since days before the decree.
  • For society: journalists, researchers and communities can check any area and month, and download the evidence with its citation.
  • Scientifically: the project addresses the sensor discontinuity that makes long-term satellite fire comparisons unreliable, with a method that extends beyond Peru.
  • NINA is a tool for historical context. Following FIRMS guidance, it is not meant for tactical or local-scale decisions.

How is it creative?

  • No public product we know of offers a validated MODIS→VIIRS bridge for fire-hotspot counts, or a detected-versus-reported comparison for Peru.
  • NINA prefers abstention to a convincing but wrong number.
  • Users can watch the sensor jump disappear: the Lab shows the harmonized series and the raw sensor side by side on the same map.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific honesty: published error, missing data never shown as zero, experimental status stated.
  • Sensor lifecycles: the end of S-NPP and the retirement of MODIS.
  • Sampling bias in daily series, and confidence used only as a filter.
  • All times kept in UTC.
  • FIRMS legal citation kept in the UI and in every export.
  • Accessible colors and a bilingual interface.
  • Reproducibility: every figure is regenerated by a script.

Tools, languages and software

  • Python 3.14 (server and processing): FastAPI, Uvicorn, DuckDB (database), NumPy, SciPy, Shapely, httpx; tests with pytest.
  • Harmonization pipeline (Python 3.12, uv): H3, Polars, pandas, PyArrow/Parquet, GeoPandas, pyogrio, statsmodels, jsonschema.
  • Frontend (TypeScript): React 19, Vite, CesiumJS (3D globe), lucide-react icons.
  • Infrastructure: Docker, Fly.io (deployment), Git/GitHub with GitHub Actions (CI).
  • Hardware: standard laptops only; NINA uses publicly available satellite data.

Use of AI

NINA does not use AI to detect or predict fires; its core is statistical calibration and geospatial analysis.

The in-app assistant answers questions from the computed evidence with a deterministic engine. An optional LLM adapter may rephrase the answers, but every number comes from the deterministic engine.

During development, the team used AI coding assistants (Claude Code) for code generation, review, debugging and documentation. All calibration results, validation metrics and datasets are produced by the project's reproducible pipeline.
